messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache paging surge detected for runtime-continuous-batching in us-west-2 at 2026-03-15T04:13:09Z (ts 1893456789). Eviction-rate up ~18x, sustained paging, error-rate bump on streaming paths.
jen_oncall: I'm oncall — triaging now. Observed nodes hitting >90% RSS and swap churn on a subset of GPU hosts. Marking high P1 due to customer-facing latency.
mike_infra: grabbing dmesg and kernel page-in stats from affected hosts. Quick paste:```
[04:12:58] host-gpu-07 kernel: node0: pages scanned 129873, reclaim 120412
[04:12:59] host-gpu-07 runtime: kv_cache: evict key=conv-512-12345 size=94MB reason=cache_pressure
[04:13:05] host-gpu-08 runtime: kv_cache: evict key=chat-history-987 size=128MB
```
sara_ml: pinging — we rolled batching config to canary yesterday afternoon. The default continuous_batch_time_ms got bumped from 10 -> 40 for higher throughput. Could amplify cache retention since more partial contexts are being retained.
dave_runtime: seeing correlated token cadence stalls on streaming connections: clients report long pauses then burst of tokens. Metrics show token_rate dropped to ~0.4 tokens/sec on some shards, and partial-flush events spiking. Hypothesis: KV cache eviction + slow IO causes partial flush to stall the generator and hold batches.
jen_oncall: OK plan: 1) Immediately revert continuous_batch_time_ms to 10 for runtime-continuous-batching on prod us-west-2 canary pool. 2) Apply a temporary per-key size cap (cap_kv_entry_bytes=65536) to avoid huge contexts. 3) Roll a rolling restart on 3 affected nodes after configs applied. 4) Add a short-term route-level circuit: disable continuous batching for top streaming-heavy customer routes.
mike_infra: I can patch config via cluster-config and trigger rollout. Command I'm about to run:```bash
# patch canary config
kubectl -n runtime patch cm continuous-batch-config -p '{"data":{"continuous_batch_time_ms":"10","cap_kv_entry_bytes":"65536"}}'
# trigger rolling restart for runtime pods
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/runtime-continuous-batching --selector=pool=us-west-2-canary
```
jen_oncall: do it, mike. I'll prepare metrics and customer notices. @carol_support can you draft an outbound for impacted customers? Keep wording cautious — degraded latency, no data loss.
carol_support: drafting now. Notifying three Dedicated customers and posting an advisory to status.redwood.ai. Rough text: "We observed elevated latency and streaming stalls in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress; we will follow up with timeline and RCA."
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/runtime-continuous-batching -> replicaset/runtime-continuous-batching-20260315b (initiated by mike_infra). Rolling restart: batch 1/4 pods restarted.
mike_infra: patch applied, verifing config on pods:```json
{"continuous_batch_time_ms":"10","cap_kv_entry_bytes":"65536"}
```
jen_oncall: seeing mem drop on host-gpu-07 within 90s of restart, evictions rate down to ~2x baseline, paging reduced. Token cadence on streaming improved on that shard.
dave_runtime: confirmed on logs — partial-flush events fell from 240/min to 12/min for the restarted pods. Consumers reporting smoothing of token flow.
jen_oncall: customer impact so far: 3 Dedicated customers with heavier streaming workloads saw increased error retries and elevated tail latencies (p95 increased from ~300ms to ~2s) for a 22-minute window before mitigation began. No reported data corruption.
sara_ml: follow-up: we should revert the canary change across the cluster and start a measured experiment to test throughput-vs-cache tradeoff with synthetic loads. I can own the eval tomorrow.
mike_infra: rolling restart finished. All canaries back on continuous_batch_time_ms=10. Monitoring dashboards: eviction_rate trending back to baseline.
jen_oncall: putting temporary rule in place: if kv_cache_evictions_rate > 5x baseline for >5m, auto-disable continuous batching on affected routes and page infra. I've opened a ticket with ops-runbook id: RB-2026-0315-CACHE.
carol_support: sent status update to customers and posted incident note on status page (initial). Will await final RCA.
dave_runtime: note for RCA: investigate partial flush edge-case where batch flush waits on KV read futures that are blocked by high page-in latency — we might need a bounded timeout on KV reads to fail-fast and trigger smaller flushes.
jen_oncall: agreed. Immediate action items assigned: - mike_infra: monitor eviction and paging metrics for next 3h and be ready to scale up nodes. - sara_ml: run workload eval + quantify perf cliff by EOD PST. - dave_runtime: implement KV read timeout prototype on staging. - carol_support: owner for customer comms. I'll hand off in 40m.
mike_infra: monitoring: dashboards -> https://grafana.internal/r/kv-evictions?org=redwood (watching).
jen_oncall: quick status for next oncall: last_message_ts=1893457099 — throttles lifted, continuous batching restored to safe default, eviction rates recovering but not fully stable. If you take over, watch token cadence and paging, and be ready to scale or disable continuous batching per the RB-2026-0315-CACHE playbook.
carol_support: final: customers acknowledged advisory. No further escalations at this time.
jen_oncall: handing off to night shift (team): SUMMARY: cache blowup caused by canary increase in continuous_batch_time_ms -> increased retained contexts -> large KV entries -> paging -> partial flush stalls -> streaming token cadence degradation. HOTFIX applied: revert batch_time, cap kv entry size, rolling restart. Next: RCA + safe experimentation plan. :white_check_mark:
